Bitcoin Market Analysis

Open thread • Replies: 12 • Updated: 2026-11-21 08:30 UTC

OP

I'm 35 (millenial), from EU, I've been in crypto since 2017, the rest of the assets since 2022. Here is my analysis of the Bitcoin market.

MARKET DESCRIPTION
1. BTC is a boom&bust asset with superior frequency and amplitude. Its performance is judged not based on YTD (year to date), but trough-to-peak, but also peak-to-trough.
2. BTC has a history of ~70% drawdowns peak-to-trough. We're at -55%.
3. Market is extremely oversold, and fear is extreme.

WHAT DO I DO
1. $95000 I stopped trading and started spot accumulating
2. If market=$40ks, ready to deploy more money
3. No plan to sell until ATH (2-5 yrs?)

WHAT NEXT
1. Investing means you'll stare at big red loss numbers for a long time. Get used to this. I'm -22% on BTC. But I have some company stocks (like Goodyear) that I see -75% and I'm not selling these.
2. At some point you'll run out of cash to invest = that's okay, you have time

WHAT DID I DO WRONG
1. $62k-$88k rally caught me off guard (that's the wrong part), because I was bearish. I deployed a lot over $70k which is OK.
2. I love Bitcoin Cash. I spent money on it. It's my pet coin.

WHAT DID I DO RIGHT
1. Jan2026 gold rally&crash = so 2026 is not gonna be normal = stop using leverage. That was right
2. Bear market rallies are not short
3. Longer bear market = ability to deploy little by little over time

MACRO CONTEXT
1. DXY and US10Y pressure the market. Warsh is hawkish on inflation, rest of FED agrees, Trump got annihilated in mid terms and Democrats are putting brakes on AI spending, Kospi collapsed, Japan has a JPY problem, and Europe stares at fiscal crisis with France potentially going full Greece.
2. Dollar is getting weaker, but in DXY it's getting stronger, because it's 50%+ euro and the euro is threatened. The dollar's power and meaning is defined by the euro, not the US.

TL;DR
If you're a zoomer or younger:
Stop panicking, hold everything you've got, and get ready to starte at unrealised losses for a long time.
Don't use leverage.

When gold kissed $3500, I started deploying money not only into BTC, but also into gold (IGLN etc), silver (ISLN), platinum (IPLT), palladium (IPDM).

The problem with precious metals is that they have 'shorter history than bitcoin' (exaggerated statement):
- Gold history can only be traced to Nixon shock, earlier history is irrelevant
- We can't say gold "peaks 4x per century then drools on the floor for decades" because of how slow its cycles are
- Bitcoin has much faster cycles, so we understand it better

As a result, I do buy precious metals, but buying them is a bigger risk. If USA goes into recession or has a credit event and has to throttle up Quantitative Easing, BTC and risk assets are expected to fly faster. Gold may rush but it may just as well stay flat.
